discovery: Quantum simulation of strongly correlated many-body physics with ultracold atoms in optical lattices (superfluid-Mott insulator transition)

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences

nominees.name: Immanuel Bloch
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and Ludwig-Maximilians-Universitaet Muenchen

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum many-body physics
motivation: In 1998 Jaksch, Zoller and co-workers showed that ultracold bosons in an optical lattice realise the Bose-Hubbard model, making a textbook condensed-matter Hamiltonian controllable with laser light. In 2002 Greiner, Bloch and colleagues observed the quantum phase transition from a superfluid to a Mott insulator, opening the field of analogue quantum simulation. They later developed single-site-resolved quantum gas microscopes that image and control individual atoms in lattices. These advances turned optical lattices into clean, tunable laboratories for strongly correlated matter, including magnetism, Fermi-Hubbard physics, many-body localisation and entanglement dynamics. The same lattice platform underpins today's most precise atomic clocks and neutral-atom quantum processors. This is a decisive, widely reproduced achievement that has united atomic physics, condensed-matter physics and quantum information.
